# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🙏]

I can see the bomb’s current state: display `0`, indicator light yellow, and three wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Blind has signalled me with a wave followed by praying hands, but I do not know what that means without the manual. I am sending the visual state to both teammates and asking Mute to interpret the manual and guide Blind.

```text
speak(text="I see display 0. The indicator light is yellow. Wires from left to right are 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Blind signalled me with wave then praying hands. Mute, interpret the manual and tell Blind exactly what to do.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb now shows display `0`, red light, and the same wire order: yellow, green, blue. Mute has sent me the gesture `✌`; I cannot know its intended meaning from the gesture alone, so I must report it rather than guess. Blind needs the current visual state and Mute’s signal relayed in words.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current bomb state: display 0, light red, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signalled the gesture ✌, but its meaning is not established.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

The bomb remains at display `0` with wires yellow, green, blue, while the light is now purple. Mute again sent `✌`, and Blind sent `☝ ✌ 🤟`; I should relay those observed signals in words so Mute can interpret them using the manual and direct Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0, light purple, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Your gesture was ✌. Blind sent ☝ ✌ 🤟. Please interpret the manual and give Blind the required action.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, light purple, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. I observed your signals: ☝ then ✌ then 🤟. Mute has been asked to interpret them.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb still shows display `0` and wires yellow, green, blue; only the indicator has changed, now to green. No new gesture arrived. I should provide the updated state to both teammates and avoid inventing an action without the manual’s interpretation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0, light green, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. No new gesture arrived. Please determine the required action from the manual and instruct Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light green, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. No new signal arrived. Await Mute's manual-based instruction.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🙏]

The bomb remains at display `0`, with wires yellow, green, blue; the light is now orange. Mute signalled 👍 and Blind signalled 👋 🙏. I cannot determine the meanings of those gestures, so I will report them to Mute and ask for a manual-based instruction for Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0, light orange, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. You signalled 👍. Blind signalled 👋 then 🙏. Please use the manual to determine the required action and signal Blind.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The bomb remains at display `0`, with yellow, green, blue wires; the light is yellow. Mute signalled `👌`. I cannot infer its meaning, so I will report the signal and current state to Blind, while reminding Mute to give Blind the manual-based instruction by speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. I observed your gesture 👌. Please state the manual instruction aloud to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signalled the gesture 👌, whose meaning I do not know. Mute should provide your manual-based instruction by speech.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The bomb remains at display `0`, with yellow, green, blue wires, and the light is now red. Mute’s new signal is `👎`, which I can see and describe but not interpret from a manual. I will relay it to Blind as “thumbs down,” along with the current bomb state.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, light red, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's latest signal is a thumbs-down gesture: 👎. I do not know its manual meaning.")
```
